official.description: The Banach NAWA programme offers scholarships for full-time second-cycle studies conducted in Polish or English at universities supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education. NAWA states the programme's goal is to support the socio-economic development of developing countries by improving the level of education and professional qualifications of their citizens; it is a joint initiative of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and NAWA implemented as Polish development cooperation. NAWA publishes the offer as a monthly scholarship of PLN 2,500, exemption from tuition fees at public universities, a PLN 2,500 travel allowance, a NAWA-funded preparatory course on the Polish track and a Polish language and culture course on the English track.
official.program_type: Government scholarship programme for second-cycle studies (Polish development aid, joint initiative of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and NAWA)
official.english_requirement: English at a minimum level of B2 documented by a certificate from the List of Recognized English Language Certificates (Attachment 4 to the call) is required to begin second-cycle studies in English; applicants must also meet the university's own language requirements during admission.
official.living_cost_coverage_note: The monthly scholarship of PLN 2,500 is the published living-cost support; NAWA does not state additional housing or insurance support.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a fully funded master's route into Poland for citizens of 36 listed countries, but the 2026/27 round closed on 8 May 2026, so the realistic target is the next annual call (announced each spring). Winning depends far more on your first-cycle grade average (up to 70 of 110 points) than on any essay, and the call can shut early once 300 applications arrive in your country group, so treat the published date as a ceiling, not a safe deadline. You must run two processes in parallel: the NAWA application and a genuine registration in the admission system of a framework-agreement university.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent (2024 or later) first-cycle graduates from the 36 listed countries with strong grades who want a tuition-free English- or Polish-taught master's in Poland and can secure university admission quickly.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your citizenship is in the 36-country list and note which of the four application groups you fall into (groups 1-3 cap at 300 applications, group 4 at 200)
Shortlist programmes from the Attachment 2 framework-agreement universities (study.gov.pl) that match your language track and register in that university's online admission system
Order a diploma supplement showing the arithmetic average grade, or a final-semester certificate with the university stamp listing all completed subjects and grades
Book a language certificate from NAWA's recognised lists (English B2 for the English track; Polish B1 for the preparatory-course path)
Record the 1-3 minute self-presentation video in Polish or English explaining your study choice and motivation, with no third parties on screen
Get non-Polish/English documents translated by a sworn translator or a Polish diplomatic mission before the call opens
common_rejection_risks: Grade average below the threshold: you need at least 50 of the 70 points for criterion 1, and below that your self-presentation is never even scored

Applying without any admission evidence: NAWA accepts an admission decision, promise/letter of acceptance, proof of admission-process participation, or documented contact with the university - no admission document at all is fatal
A language certificate that is not on NAWA's recognised lists, or a level below B2 for the chosen study language
Missing the per-group application cap: groups 1-3 close after 300 applications and group 4 after 200, whatever the calendar says
Choosing the Polish path with the preparatory course when you cannot meet the B1 requirement, or expecting to switch tracks later - the path choice is binding
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The published package covers tuition at public universities, PLN 2,500 per month and a PLN 2,500 travel lump sum; fees at private universities are not covered, and NAWA states nothing about visa, insurance or accommodation costs, so those and any living costs above the monthly stipend are self-funded.
document_audit: Diploma must come from a Programme country and be no older than 2024, with an average-grade supplement - a bare diploma scan is insufficient
Final-semester students need the university-issued certificate on the official template with stamp, average grade and full subject list, not an informal email
The video must be 1-3 minutes in Polish or English, justify the field of study and motivation, and contain no images of third parties
A recommendation letter from a Polish diplomatic mission is optional but worth up to 10 points - request it early through your local mission
alerts: The 8 May 2026 deadline passed; monitor the NAWA Banach page and programme schedule for the next call, typically announced in spring for the following winter semester
Applications in your country group can close the call early (300 in groups 1-3, 200 in group 4), so submit as soon as the call opens
If awarded, the scholarship agreement must be signed within 45 days of it appearing in the NAWA IT system
An annual report is due by 31 October each year after completing an academic year under the Programme
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Secure university admission or admission-process confirmation, upload all attachments to the NAWA IT system in Polish or English before the deadline or group cap, then await the July results and sign the agreement if awarded.

benefits: employment of foreign researchers for a period from 6 to 24 months
remuneration of the Principal Investigator in the maximum amount of PLN 17,000 per month in case of full-time employment, including employer costs (gross gross)
remuneration of the Inviting Person in the form of a task allowance in the maximum amount of PLN 1,200 per month

simplified special track for Seal of Excellence (MSCA PF-EF) and Accolade of Excellence (MSCA4Ukraine) certificate holders, whose European certificates NAWA recognises as binding verification of application quality
open to all fields of science, all ages and all countries of origin, including Polish scientists working permanently abroad (maximum 10% of funded Principal Investigators)
eligibility: Applicant must be a Polish higher education institution, scientific or research institute or other authorised entity under art. 7 par. 1 points 1, 2 and 4-7 of the Act of 20 July 2018 (Law on Higher Education and Science)
Principal Investigator holds at least a doctoral degree or equivalent degree obtained abroad at the time of the application deadline

Principal Investigator is employed at a foreign university or foreign scientific/research centre, or the last such employment ended after 31 August 2025 (employment not required for those who obtained the doctoral degree after 31 August 2025)
Principal Investigator had not worked nor studied in Poland in the 3 years before the application deadline and had not stayed in Poland continuously for longer than 3 months in that period

Principal Investigator has at least 3 achievements within 5 years before the call deadline: English-language main-author publications in Scopus, Science Citation Index Expanded, Social Sciences Citation Index or Arts & Humanities Citation Index journals; a peer-reviewed English-language monograph; peer-reviewed CORE/DBLP-indexed or Web of Science/Scopus-indexed international conference publications; or, for art sciences, confirmed presentations or international competition awards
citizens of the Russian Federation and entities based in the Russian Federation are excluded from the Programme

the Host institution implements the European Charter for Researchers: office and laboratory space, research equipment and infrastructure access, administrative and financial support, support in applying for research funding and in obtaining necessary permits

scan of the document confirming the Principal Investigator is a PhD holder, with official translation into English if the original is not in English or Polish

certificate from the HR department or an employer representative confirming the Principal Investigator's research employment outside Poland, with position and period of employment, in English
copies of the three required achievements from the last five years

attachments in electronic form as scans with handwritten signature or documents with a qualified electronic signature

scoring: maximum 100 points (Team of Experts initial 20, External Reviewers 40, final Team of Experts 40); applications without the Team of Experts' initial recommendation are not assessed further

official.application_route: A Polish host institution applies on the researcher's behalf, electronically in English via NAWA's ICT system at https://programs.nawa.gov.pl; individual researchers cannot apply directly.
official.study_mode: full-time employment (part-time possible in justified cases with proportionally reduced Programme financing, as published)
official.citizenship_residency: No country-of-origin limit for the Principal Investigator (all disciplines, all ages, including Polish scientists working permanently abroad, capped at 10% of funded Principal Investigators); citizens of the Russian Federation and Russia-based entities are excluded; the applicant institution must be based in Poland.
official.international_eligibility: Researchers of any nationality except Russian citizens may be invited; the applying and funding entity must be a Polish institution.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Open to all fields of science; representatives of the arts are eligible provided the planned Project activities are of a scientific nature. The applicant must be a Polish entity under art. 7 par. 1 points 1, 2 and 4-7 of the Law on Higher Education and Science.
official.research_requirement: The Principal Investigator must demonstrate at least 3 achievements within the 5 years before the call deadline (publications in indexed journals or peer-reviewed proceedings in English, a peer-reviewed monograph, or equivalent art-science accomplishments).
official.duration: 6 to 24 months of full-time employment at the Polish Host institution; project start between 1 February 2027 and 1 December 2027; Programme implementation period 1 February 2027 - 31 December 2030.
official.description: The Ulam NAWA Programme is an institutional programme that lets Polish higher education and research institutions employ outstanding scientists from abroad for 6 to 24 months to strengthen their scientific potential, primarily in research projects and didactics. NAWA states the programme is open to scientists regardless of age, from all around the world and representing all fields of science, and that funding covers remuneration for the Principal Investigator and the Inviting Person. A simplified special track recognises Seal of Excellence (MSCA PF-EF) and Accolade of Excellence (MSCA4Ukraine) certificates as binding verification of application quality.
official.program_type: Institutional research programme funding employment of foreign scientists at Polish institutions (NAWA)
official.english_requirement: The application must be completed in English; applications prepared in Polish will be disregarded. The power of attorney must be in Polish, and the PhD-confirming document and employment certificate must be in English or accompanied by an official English translation.

applicant_utility.summary: As a researcher you cannot apply yourself - a Polish university or research institute must invite you and file the application in English through NAWA's ICT system, so the first task is finding a host whose priorities match your profile and convincing them to name you as Principal Investigator. The funding is employment remuneration up to PLN 17,000 per month including employer costs for a 6-24 month full-time position, not a scholarship stipend, and the PI must relocate to Poland with their centre of personal and economic interests there. Check the eligibility traps before investing effort: no work or studies in Poland in the three years before the deadline, at least three indexed achievements in the last five years, and no employment in Poland between applying and the results announcement.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Doctoral-level researchers employed abroad (especially outside Poland for 3+ years) with three recent indexed publications, who can persuade a Polish HEI or research institute to host and employ them full-time.
application_readiness_checklist: Identify and contact a Polish HEI or research institute whose research priorities fit your profile and confirm they are eligible to apply under the Law on Higher Education and Science

Verify the PI window: doctoral degree held at the deadline, foreign employment (or degree obtained after 31 August 2025), and no work, studies or continuous stays over 3 months in Poland in the 3 years before the deadline
Document at least three achievements from the five years before the deadline (indexed English-language publications, monograph, indexed conference proceedings, or art-science equivalents)
Agree project scope, employment conditions and the supporting Inviting Person with the host, and have the host issue the signed invitation on NAWA's template
Have the host prepare the power of attorney in Polish and obtain official English translations of the PhD document and the HR employment certificate
Ensure you appear in only one application and take no employment in Poland before the results announcement
common_rejection_risks: Assuming you can apply directly - applications come only from the inviting Polish institution, and there is no route for individual researchers
Application prepared in Polish: NAWA states Polish applications will be disregarded regardless of quality
Failing the 3-year Poland window: recent work, studies or a continuous stay over 3 months in Poland disqualifies the PI unless they hold a Seal of Excellence or Accolade of Excellence (special track)
Duplicate applications naming the same PI - only the most recently submitted one is assessed and the rest are discarded
Taking any Polish employment between submission and the results announcement, which voids the funding agreement condition

Fewer than three qualifying achievements in the five-year window, or achievements not matching the listed categories (indexed journals, monograph, CORE/DBLP or Web of Science/Scopus proceedings, art-science equivalents)
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Funding covers PI remuneration up to PLN 17,000 per month including employer costs and an Inviting Person task allowance up to PLN 1,200 per month; the call publishes nothing about travel, relocation, housing or insurance support, so those remain unfunded. The host must supply office/laboratory space and infrastructure under the European Charter commitments.
document_audit: The power of attorney must be in Polish on the call's template - an English or self-drafted version fails formality
The employment certificate must come from the HR department or an employer representative and state the position and period, in English
PhD proof needs an official English translation unless the original is already in English or Polish
Special-track applicants must attach the original MSCA application, the reviews and the award itself, not just the certificate
alerts: The 2026 call closed on 15 May 2026 at 3:00 p.m. Poland time; results are due by 30 November 2026 and the next call has not yet been announced
Projects must start between 1 February and 1 December 2027 under the Programme window ending 31 December 2030 - plan the employment start accordingly
Polish citizens can fill at most 10% of funded PI places, and Russian citizens and Russia-based entities are excluded entirely
Part-time employment is possible only in justified cases and reduces Programme financing proportionally
Seal of Excellence (MSCA PF-EF) and Accolade of Excellence (MSCA4Ukraine) holders can use the simplified special track, which bypasses the remaining PI requirements including the 3-year Poland window
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: The host institution files in NAWA's ICT system at programs.nawa.gov.pl in English by the call deadline, NAWA runs formal and three-stage merit review, and awarded hosts sign the Beneficiary Agreement and employ the PI full-time within the 1 February - 1 December 2027 start window.
